question.text: The expression $2^{4 n}-15 n-1$, where $n \in \mathbb{N}$ (the set of natural numbers) is divisible by

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { } 2^{4 n}-15 n-1=(1+15)^n-15 n-1=\left({ }^n C_0+{ }^n C_1 \cdot 15+{ }^n C_2 15^2+\ldots \ldots \ldots . .+{ }^n C_n \cdot 15^n\right)-15 n-1 \\ & =15^2\left({ }^n C_2+{ }^n C_3 \cdot 15 \ldots \ldots \ldots .+{ }^n C_n \cdot 15^{n-2}\right) \\ & =225 K, K \in \mathbb{N}\end{aligned}$
